fields.description:
Mirror inventory finding F2 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), MEDIUM.

## Problem

The op-cert kind vocabulary has three masters:

- `src/rebar/signing.py:115` `OPCERT_KINDS` — canonical, and already EXPORTED in `__all__` at `:76`
- `src/rebar/opcert_service/jobs.py:38` `VALID_KINDS` — the same two, hand-copied
- `src/rebar/_commands/remote_cert.py:24` `_VALID_KINDS` — the same two again, plus a prose copy
  in `_USAGE` at `:23`

Neither consumer imports the exported name, and both gate client REQUEST VALIDATION: a kind
present in `OPCERT_KINDS` but missing from a consumer's copy is silently rejected as invalid.
Churn is low — ADR 0049 fixes the count at two — which is precisely why a miss would sit
unnoticed.

## The consumers, and why a naive import would be WRONG

`OPCERT_KINDS` is a `frozenset` — UNORDERED. Both copies are ordered TUPLES, and three
consumers depend on that:

- `_cli/_parsers/advanced/certs.py:51` — `choices=remote_cert._VALID_KINDS`. argparse renders
  `choices` into help and into its error text, so a frozenset makes both non-deterministic.
- `opcert_service/app.py:222` — `f"kind must be one of {list(jobs.VALID_KINDS)}"`, an
  order-visible API error message.
- `opcert_service/__init__.py:14,18` — re-exports `VALID_KINDS` in `__all__`. It is PUBLIC
  API, so changing its type is a breaking change independent of ordering.

(`app.py:217` is a membership test and is indifferent.)

## Approach — generate-from-canonical, preserving type and order

Both copies become `tuple(sorted(OPCERT_KINDS))`. Sorted order is
`("completion-verifier", "plan-review")` — byte-identical to what both copies hold today, so
every consumer above sees exactly what it sees now, while the MEMBERSHIP stops being a
hand-copy. `_USAGE` prose is generated from the same tuple.

Deriving a frozenset here would have been the wrong fix, and that is the substance of this
ticket: the canonical value and its consumers disagree about whether order is part of the fact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: both copies are derived from `signing.OPCERT_KINDS` and neither re-lists the kinds.
      Verified by a test asserting each equals `tuple(sorted(OPCERT_KINDS))` and the literals are gone.
- [ ] AC1b: both remain ORDERED TUPLES with their current order, so argparse `choices`, the
      `app.py:222` error message and the `opcert_service.__all__` export are unchanged. Verified by
      a test asserting the exact tuple value and its type.
- [ ] AC2: `remote_cert`'s `_USAGE` names exactly the canonical kinds, generated not re-typed.
      Verified by a test comparing the usage text against the set.
- [ ] AC3: a kind added to `OPCERT_KINDS` is accepted by both consumers with no further edit.
      Verified by a test that patches the canonical set and asserts both validators follow.
- [ ] AC4: an unknown kind is still rejected at both sites. Verified by explicit rejection tests.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "opcert or remote_cert or signing" -q` — AC1-AC4.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
